scope_note: Current registered product surface only, reconciled at the recorded candidate. All commands remain Unverified against restored UX rules. Approved consent changes are implementation gaps, not current signatures or compliance exceptions. Internal/framework surfaces and retired-command rejection checks are separate.

contracts.current_json: Preserve current command-specific success DTOs and error.code/message/details?/request_id. Do not copy legacy success.data/meta or error.meta envelopes.
contracts.typed_http: Operational requests remain typed SDK HTTP calls. Do not add SSH, remote shell or generic executors to product commands. Explicit local trust/DNS and local profile/extension operations retain their bounded adapters.
contracts.existing_signature: Current command signatures are exact-tested. Record intentional input or consent changes explicitly; do not assume legacy prompting or --force semantics.
contracts.local_profile: Uses local Orbit profile configuration rather than an operational Gateway request.
contracts.active_profile_force: --force permits removing the active profile and clearing active selection; it is not merely a generic confirmation bypass.
contracts.trust_local: Explicit visible local trust operation. --accept-ca-change accepts a changed Gateway CA; preserve this distinct trust decision.
contracts.dns_local: Explicit visible local resolver operation. --reset selects resolver reset behavior; do not reinterpret it as consent.
contracts.extension_local: Uses private local extension state. Herdr command visibility and invocation guards change when the extension is enabled or disabled.
contracts.numeric_target: Current signature accepts an explicit positive numeric resource ID; generic prompting must not silently change identifier semantics.
contracts.cluster_consent: Interactive confirmation defaults to No; JSON/noninteractive removal requires --force.
contracts.node_reference: Where supported, Node reference resolution accepts positive numeric ID or exact registered name through Gateway lookup.
contracts.node_remove_consent: Resolve the existing Node before requiring consent. Missing targets must remain not-found rather than consent-required. Interactive confirmation defaults to No; --force supplies consent.
contracts.node_offline: --offline is a separate explicit operational claim, not a consent flag.
contracts.node_role_consent: Role removal has existing preview/confirmation behavior. Preserve --force, --purge-data and --offline distinctions.
contracts.node_access: Consumer and serving Nodes are explicit numeric IDs. CLI does not decide access, Gateway identity or role authority.
contracts.node_access_consent: Access removal requires default-No interactive confirmation or --force.
contracts.instance_force_override: --force authorizes dirty/unpublished source deletion after identity checks. Do not conflate source-safety override with ordinary destructive consent.
contracts.source_recovery: --recover-source-profile controls explicit source-profile recovery, not generic consent.
contracts.registration: Registration examines source facts and may prompt for unresolved default branch/root; noninteractive registration requires unresolved values as options. Ownership transfer is a separate confirmation decision.
contracts.database_secret: Database configuration may receive passwords, but ordinary result output must preserve credential redaction and password-presence semantics.
contracts.database_consent: Default-No interactive confirmation or --force is required for database destruction or attachment removal.
contracts.attachment_target: Requires explicit --instance targeting; attachment prefix and database slug are separate inputs.
contracts.environment_explicit: Explicit numeric AppInstance ID or exact Route domain only. Never select a target, display values, read/write local environment files, resolve placeholders, restart processes or refresh application caches.
contracts.environment_replace: --replace permits stored-key conflicts during import; preserve existing values otherwise.
contracts.environment_strings: Preserve quoted empty, multiline, false, zero and placeholder-containing values as strings.
contracts.definition_target: App-owned runtime definitions and concrete runtime resources are distinct. Preserve --app/--for and current ID/name targeting rules.
contracts.process_target: Preserve process target exclusivity and current App/Node/AppInstance behavior; do not add target discovery through generic UX helpers.
contracts.bounded_process_logs: One bounded log tail with --lines 1..1000; no continuous follow stream. Preserve log sanitization and request ID.
contracts.schedule_explicit: schedule:create requires exactly one of --app, --node or --instance in every mode. Never discover or prompt for a target. App definitions require --for; --no-start is AppInstance-only.
contracts.schedule_uuid: Concrete Schedule operations use a Schedule UUID, distinct from App definition names.
contracts.schedule_no_complete: Completion is internal Node-authenticated API/SDK transport. Never expose schedule:complete.
contracts.bounded_schedule_logs: One bounded log tail with --lines 1..1000; no continuous follow stream.
contracts.tool_install_prompt: Node remains explicit. Interactive manager choices come from that Node's supported active/uninstalled managers. Missing package may be prompted. JSON/noninteractive calls must supply Node, manager and package.
contracts.tool_gateway_policy: Tool manager execution, SemVer policy and infrastructure remain Gateway responsibilities.
contracts.metrics_enable_prompt: metrics:enable permits Node selection when omitted in human interactive mode. JSON and noninteractive input must provide the target. Node ID or exact registered name remains accepted.
contracts.metrics_disable: Noninteractive/JSON disable requires --force. --purge-data also requires --force; interactive nonforced disable shows preview and default-No confirmation.
contracts.metrics_credentials: Explicit credential-delivery command intentionally returns URL, username and password. --reset rotates the password. This is an exception to ordinary secret-free output, and proof must use disposable credentials with controlled artifacts.
contracts.herdr_enabled: Supported public command only when Herdr extension is enabled; hidden and guarded otherwise.
contracts.herdr_target: Requires explicit session name and Node reference; resolves the named session through the Gateway.
contracts.herdr_destroy: --accept-termination explicitly accepts live-pane termination. Destruction removes the session from Orbit and destroys its Process only when Orbit manages it.
contracts.herdr_restart: --handoff requests live handoff only when inspected server support permits it.
contracts.herdr_grant: Issues a short-lived receive-only observation grant rather than attaching a CLI stream. Requires pane, terminal, viewport and HTTPS origin. Intentionally returns observer URL; handle proof artifacts accordingly.
contracts.doctor_sync: Verify-only synchronous read-only comparison. No repair, adoption, progress stream or persisted run. Local liveness must not invent remote milestones or percentage.
contracts.doctor_scope: Preserve selected scope, family ordering, bounded findings, resource-based checked counts, and unhealthy exit status. Current families: node, role, app, instance, schedule, tool, process, firewall, herdr, database_connection. The retired workspace family is not supported after ORB-204.
contracts.deployment_ndjson: --json already emits NDJSON phase/output/result records with sequence and request_id. Do not replace with a final envelope or require --stream-json without an explicit compatibility decision.
contracts.deployment_bytes: JSON output bytes use data_base64; current human bytes use escaped terminal-safe strings. Preserve binary/control-character safety and result-derived exit status.
contracts.deployment_failure: Retain partial stream evidence, close stream on exit, and distinguish terminal result failure from malformed/interrupted stream.
contracts.vocabulary: Use accepted ADR 0071 and the current vocabulary. Do not reintroduce retired Workspace or deployment document/layout commands.
contracts.approved_destructive_consent: User-approved migration: default-No consent or --yes on previously unconfirmed destructive paths, including source ownership transfer. Existing consent flags and force overrides retain their meanings. Current signatures below remain observed baseline, not migrated behavior.

known_gaps.app_destroy_no_consent: Approved migration: require default-No destructive consent or explicit --yes, preserving target validation and existing override semantics. Current source has no independent consent; this remains an implementation gap.
known_gaps.process_no_consent: Approved migration: require default-No destructive consent or explicit --yes, preserving target validation and existing override semantics. Current source has no independent consent; this remains an implementation gap.
known_gaps.route_no_consent: Approved migration: require default-No destructive consent or explicit --yes, preserving target validation and existing override semantics. Current source has no independent consent; this remains an implementation gap.
known_gaps.schedule_no_consent: Approved migration: require default-No destructive consent or explicit --yes, preserving target validation and existing override semantics. Current source has no independent consent; this remains an implementation gap.
known_gaps.tool_no_consent: Approved migration: require default-No destructive consent or explicit --yes, preserving target validation and existing override semantics. Current source has no independent consent; this remains an implementation gap.
known_gaps.firewall_no_consent: Approved migration: require default-No destructive consent or explicit --yes, preserving target validation and existing override semantics. Current source has no independent consent; this remains an implementation gap.
known_gaps.registration_default_yes: Approved migration: default-No ownership transfer and explicit --yes automation consent. Current source defaults Yes and has no --yes; preserve instance.registration_cancelled when implementing the approved change.
known_gaps.metrics_open_target_prompt: Metrics enable prints eligible Nodes then asks for an open-text Node identity; replace with the chosen finite registry-selection primitive.
known_gaps.legacy_prompt_calls: Command or shared family helper uses Symfony ask/choice/confirm instead of the restored prompt primitives.
known_gaps.legacy_table_call: Command directly renders a Symfony table; migrate to the documented table/detail primitive while preserving command-specific fields.
known_gaps.shared_gateway_wait: GatewayCommand send/sendOrThrow blocks without a shared visible wait indicator. Slow-request paths need truthful terminal liveness; fast reads may not need a progress surface.
known_gaps.generic_detail_layout: Detail command uses line-oriented or Field/Value table output and requires review against the restored detail primitive.
known_gaps.machine_mode_audit: Global quiet/silent/verbosity and decoration behavior must be checked with machine output before claiming conformance.
known_gaps.deploy_step_no_consent: Current instance:deploy-step:destroy deletes a named deploy step without consent. Approved migration adds default-No consent or --yes.
known_gaps.gateway_remove_no_independent_consent: Approved migration: gateway:remove needs default-No or --yes consent; existing --force separately permits active-profile removal. Not implemented in this source.
known_gaps.instance_destroy_no_independent_consent: Approved migration: instance:destroy needs default-No or --yes consent; existing --force separately permits dirty/unpublished source removal. Not implemented in this source.

observed_behaviors.plain_list: Existing list is read-only. Decide any interactive navigation from current command requirements; existing table rendering is an observation, not a permanent exemption.

verification_gaps.terminal_proof: Real Solo/PTY evidence has not been collected for this command. Automated output assertions do not prove interaction, redraw or liveness.
